jobs.excerpt: Who We Are:We are a tech-enabled growth firm–at the intersection of marketing, consulting & data intelligence–igniting revenue and brand recognition for leading and emerging companies around the world.
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

We are a tech-enabled growth firm–at the intersection of marketing, consulting & data intelligence–igniting revenue and brand recognition for leading and emerging companies around the world. As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. Our vision is to be recognized as the most valued and respected private growth marketing firm in the world–with a scalable brand, culture and services. Our mission is to power the relentless pursuit of growth and redefine what’s possible through a team of growth-obsessed experts who demand innovation and results - driven by integrity, autonomy, and grit.

As a full-service growth marketing firm, we offer best-in-class services including: SEO, Content Marketing, Paid Media, Social Media Marketing, Programmatic + CTV, Public Relations, Influencer Marketing, Email + SMS, Conversion Rate Optimization, Retail Marketing, and Creative. Here at Power Digital, we are hyper-focused on helping brands drive revenue growth and brand recognition, ultimately driving irrefutable value for our clients.

At the heart of Power Digital is our proprietary technology, nova, which analyzes businesses through first-party data, simplifying investment planning for marketing and diligence in M&A––putting marketers in a strategic seat at the table––and providing value in unparalleled ways.

Managing billions in media, our dynamic team––of consultative marketers, creatives, analysts and technologists––challenge traditional ways of planning and measurement through meticulous testing and data science across each milestone of the customer journey.

**We support 100% remote, in-office, or hybrid work styles for anyone legally eligible to work in the U.S.

A day in the life:

The Director of GTM, Partnerships is a mid to senior-level role at the center of Power Digital's Partnerships team, responsible for translating the partner ecosystem (Tech, PE and Advisors) into measurable commercial value. This person owns the full commercial lifecycle across our partner go-to-market. This is a highly cross-functional, enterprise-facing role that requires equal parts relationship builder, strategic operator, and financial thinker. You will manage complex fundraising motions, own commercial revenue streams from ideation to negotiation, and serve as the bridge between partners and Power Digital's internal product, sales, CX, and marketing teams.

This role reports directly to the VP of Partnerships.

Responsibilities:

Joint GTM with the Partner Ecosystem

  • Lead new partner vetting and due diligence—evaluating whether technology solutions are the right fit for Power Digital clients based on performance data, ICP alignment, and commercial potential.
  • Develop and manage joint business plans (JBPs) with priority technology and channel partners, translating shared goals into defined initiatives, timelines, and revenue targets.
  • Own and structure commercial agreements, including co-selling arrangements, resell and white-label opportunities, and bonus media incentive programs.
  • Source and activate alpha and beta opportunities with platform partners to give Power Digital a competitive first-mover advantage for clients.
  • Design, launch, and manage partner pilot programs in coordination with internal activation and CX teams.
  • Employ AI technologies to enhance and optimize GTM processes and partner engagement workflows.
  • Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to the Partnerships function.

Fusepoint Partnerships

  • Develop and grow a portfolio of technology partnerships specifically designed to support fusepoint, Power Digital's measurement and strategic consulting practice.
  • Identify and structure partnerships that unlock exclusive testing opportunities, platform performance consulting engagements, referral programs, and client-facing competitive advantages.
  • Source credentialing and certification opportunities with platform partners that elevate FusePoint's credibility and market position.
  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for FusePoint's partner ecosystem, ensuring alignment between partner capabilities and FusePoint priorities.

Joint Technical Innovation (nova)

  • Develop and manage partnerships with technology companies aimed at co-developing nova capabilities, offsetting the product roadmap, or providing exclusive access to AI/data insights and tooling.
  • Own the full sales cycle for joint technical planning (JTP) initiatives—from opportunity identification and stakeholder alignment through proposal development, negotiation, and signed agreement.
  • Partner closely with Power Digital's product and engineering teams to ensure external partnership opportunities are aligned to the Nova roadmap and technically viable.
  • Execute a highly complex, enterprise fundraising motion—including financial modeling and reverse M&A-style structures—to secure technical funding and resource offsets from platform partners.
  • Manage executive stakeholder relationships at partner organizations, building long-term alliances that generate recurring technical investment.
  • Conduct technical demonstrations and present compelling business cases to secure JTP commitments from partner organizations.
  • Monitor emerging trends in AI, AdTech, and data infrastructure to surface new opportunities that align partner priorities with Nova's roadmap.

Reporting, Pacing & Commercial Operations

  • Own end-to-end commercial deal management: sourcing, structuring, executing, and reporting on all commercial partner agreements.
  • Track and communicate pacing toward commercial revenue targets on a monthly and quarterly basis, flagging risks and opportunities in real time.
  • Manage the distribution and re-investment of commercial deal value back to the appropriate business units (product, activation, sales/marketing, partnerships, etc.).
  • Define and maintain measurable OKRs and KPIs for all active commercial partnerships, ensuring alignment with broader organizational goals.

Program Management & Cross-Functional Execution

  • Serve as the sole internal champion for partner pilots, incentive programs, and commercial initiatives—owning the full program lifecycle from kickoff to post-delivery reporting.
  • Work cross-functionally with marketing, sales, product, and CX to ensure partner programs are fully resourced and successfully executed.
  • Act as the primary bridge between external partners and Power Digital's internal teams, managing timelines, escalations, and stakeholder communication throughout.
  • Build feedback loops from the delivery team back to partners to demonstrate performance, reinforce trust, and identify expansion opportunities.

Co-Marketing & Brand Amplification

  • Identify and secure speaking opportunities at partner-hosted events, industry conferences, and co-produced webinars—positioning Power Digital and fusepoint SMEs as thought leaders within the partner ecosystem.
  • Develop and pitch joint content opportunities with technology partners, including whitepapers, case studies, blog features, social campaigns, and co-branded research that expand reach and reinforce credibility.
  • Build and maintain a rolling co-marketing pipeline with priority partners—proactively sourcing opportunities tied to FusePoint's consulting capabilities, Nova's technology story, and Power Digital's broader service offering.
  • Coordinate with the internal marketing team to brief, scope, and execute co-marketing initiatives—ensuring partner needs are properly resourced and launched on time.
  • Pitch and secure sponsorship and activation opportunities for partners to participate in Power Digital summits, client dinners, and co-hosted events.
  • Leverage the partner ecosystem to facilitate introductions and build relationships between priority technology partners and Power Digital's CX team—creating direct lines of support that drive client retention, upsell opportunities, and deeper platform utilization across the book of business.

Role Requirements:

Skills & Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in partnerships, business development, or GTM roles—ideally within a marketing agency, AdTech, SaaS, or consulting environment.
  • Proven track record of owning and closing complex commercial agreements, including co-sell, resell, or technology partnership structures.
  • Experience with enterprise fundraising motions, joint business planning, or financial modeling
  • Deep understanding of the AdTech and MarTech landscape, including platforms such as Google, Meta, TikTok, Amazon, Snowflake, Klaviyo, Shopify, or similar.
  • Strong analytical skills—comfortable building financial models, interpreting performance data, and synthesizing market intelligence into partner strategy.
  • Excellent executive presence and presentation skills; able to command the room with both internal leadership and senior partner stakeholders.
  • Experience working cross-functionally across marketing, sales, product, and CX teams to drive shared outcomes.

jobs.description:
Metro Vein Centers is a rapidly growing healthcare practice specializing in state-of-the-art vein treatments. Our board-certified physicians and expert staff are on a mission to improve people’s quality of life by relieving the painful, yet highly treatable symptoms of vein disease—such as varicose veins and heavy, aching legs.

With over 70 clinics across 8 states, and still growing, we’re building the future of vein care—delivering compassionate, results-driven care in a modern, patient-first environment.

We proudly maintain a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 93, the highest patient satisfaction in the industry.

Role Overview

The Director of Lifecycle Marketing owns the patient lifecycle end-to-end — from first inquiry through booking, attendance, treatment completion, and reactivation. Unlike traditional retention-focused roles, this position is about preventing dropoff and accelerating the path to treatment in a high-consideration healthcare journey.

As a strategic partner to Revenue Cycle Management (RCM), Patient Intake (Sales), Tech and Data, and Operations, you'll own HubSpot as the connective tissue across these functions, define the lifecycle KPI framework, establish the testing and measurement methodology, and own governance for all patient and marketing communications.

You'll manage and develop our Lifecycle Marketing Manager, setting the strategic vision while staying close enough to the work to QA campaigns, troubleshoot workflows, and pressure-test the data.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Lifecycle Ownership & Strategic Partner

  • Own the patient lifecycle end-to-end, with strategic accountability across booking, attendance, treatment completion, and reactivation
  • Identify dropoff points across digital and offline touchpoints (email, SMS, front desk, in-clinic, direct mail) and prioritize the highest-leverage interventions at each stage
  • Translate operational realities (no-show patterns, intake bottlenecks, insurance authorization timing, post-treatment follow-up gaps) into communications strategies that drive measurable outcomes
  • Champion AI across the lifecycle function, e.g. predictive modeling (no-show, conversion, reactivation), personalization, content generation, and agentic automation for QA, deliverability monitoring, and anomaly detection
  • Partner with Ops on NPS and reputation-focused automations (review requests, survey triggers, detractor routing)
  • Partner with Tech and Data on instrumentation, integrations, data hygiene, and measurement infrastructure
  • Manage and develop the Lifecycle Marketing Manager

CRM & Marketing Automation

  • Own patient lifecycle communications and behavior within HubSpot, partnering closely with tech and data on architecture, data hygiene, integrations, and governance
  • Define the roadmap for automation, segmentation, and personalization across email, SMS, and other lifecycle channels
  • Partner with Tech and Data on integrations between HubSpot and adjacent systems (Luma, EMR, RCM platforms, intake tools)

KPIs, Testing & Incremental Lift

  • Define and own the lifecycle KPI framework, with particular focus on consult attendance, treatment completion, and patient reactivation
  • Establish the testing framework for the function, including A/B and incremental holdout testing to measure causal lift in addition to topline metrics
  • Design, instrument, and analyze experiments that distinguish lifecycle-driven impact from baseline behavior
  • Build dashboards and reporting cadences that provide a shared view of lifecycle performance and incrementality

Governance, Communications & Compliance

  • Own governance for all patient and marketing communication—channel strategy, contact frequency, message hierarchy, suppression rules, and brand voice
  • Own sender infrastructure and consent architecture across email and SMS, including domain authentication, list hygiene, preference centers, and TCPA-compliant opt-in/opt-out flows
  • Establish the operating model for how lifecycle, brand, intake, and ops teams coordinate on patient-facing messaging
  • Ensure all communications meet HIPAA, TCPA, CAN-SPAM, and state-level healthcare marketing requirements; partner with Legal/Compliance on consent management, data handling, and audit readiness
  • Stay current on healthcare marketing regulations and platform policy changes (Apple MPP, Google deliverability shifts, SMS carrier rules, etc.)

Qualifications

  • 6–8 years of lifecycle marketing experience managing complex lifecycle journeys
  • Healthcare industry experience ideal; multi-location consumer healthcare, dental, or specialty care strongly preferred
  • Proven track record of partnering with RCM, intake/sales, and operations functions
  • Strong command of lifecycle metrics and frameworks, particularly booking, attendance, completion, and reactivation
  • Proven experience building structured testing and experimentation frameworks (A/B and incremental holdout) to measure causal lift
  • Technical fluency across email and SMS infrastructure, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI), deliverability and inbox placement, 10DLC registration, carrier filtering, and IP/domain reputation management
  • Demonstrated fluency in CRM tools; HubSpot experience a plus
  • Highly analytical; fluent in Excel/Google Sheets and/or BI tools (Looker, Tableau, etc.)
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare marketing compliance
  • Proven track record of leveraging HIPAA-compliant AI as a force multiplier, predictive scoring, personalization, content generation/optimization, and agentic QA/ops automation
  • Hands-on enough to QA workflows, troubleshoot data issues, and pressure-test campaign logic
  • Familiarity with emerging messaging channels (RCS Business Messaging, branded sender verification) and a point of view on where to invest as the channel matures
  • Excellent communication skills; able to influence senior cross-functional leaders
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment with high performance expectations

The Metro Vein Centers Difference

Healthy legs. Happier lives.
At Metro Vein Centers, we believe exceptional care begins with an exceptional experience. Our mission is to make vein care approachable, empowering, and connected to overall well-being. From the first conversation to the final follow-up, every patient interaction reflects our commitment to compassion, expertise, and trust.

A team united by purpose.

Our values guide everything we do:

  • Patients First, Always – Every interaction should make our patients feel valued, heard, and cared for.
  • Stronger Together – Teamwork and collaboration drive our success. We lift each other up to deliver the best for our patients.

About the Company

Bay Business Group is an employee‑focused accounting and advisory firm that specializes in delivering high‑quality Client Accounting Services (CAS) to small businesses and nonprofits. We combine modern cloud‑based tools with practical, hands‑on support so our clients can make better decisions and spend more time on their mission. As part of our team, you’ll work in a collaborative environment that values continuous learning, clear processes, and proactive communication with clients.

About the Role

The Associate Staff Accountant will support our Client Accounting Services (CAS) team by handling day‑to‑day transactional work for multiple small business and nonprofit clients. This role is ideal for someone early in their accounting career who wants broad exposure to real‑world client books and modern cloud accounting systems.

Key Responsibilities
  • Record and code daily transactions (bank, credit card, payroll, other journals) to the correct general ledger accounts and classes based on firm and client coding rules.
  • Assist with monthly account reconciliations, including bank, credit card, loan, intercompany, and balance sheet accounts.
  • Prepare and maintain supporting schedules for key balance sheet accounts (prepaids, fixed assets, accrued expenses, deferred revenue, etc.).
  • Support accounts payable processes: enter vendor bills, verify coding and approvals, maintain vendor records, schedule payments, and help monitor AP aging.
  • Support accounts receivable processes: create and send invoices, apply customer payments, assist with collections follow‑ups, and help monitor AR aging.
  • Assist with payroll workflows: gather and validate time or pay data, upload files or entries to payroll systems, post payroll journal entries, and reconcile payroll‑related accounts.
  • Maintain organized electronic workpapers and documentation for all reconciliations and entries in accordance with firm standards.
  • Help prepare standardized monthly financial reporting packages for review by senior staff (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow summaries, and selected analytics).
  • Research and resolve basic variances or data issues under the direction of a Staff Accountant or CAS Manager, documenting findings and resolutions.
  • Communicate professionally with internal team members (and occasionally clients) via email, chat, and video to clarify transaction details and open items.
  • Contribute to process improvements by following checklists, suggesting refinements, and documenting repeatable steps in firm SOPs.

Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field (or in progress with relevant experience).
  • 2-5 years of experience in bookkeeping, accounting, or a client accounting services environment (internships and part‑time roles acceptable).
  • Solid understanding of basic accounting principles, including debits/credits and the structure of financial statements.
  • Experience with cloud accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks Online, Xero, or similar) preferred.
  • Proficiency with Excel/Google Sheets, including basic formulas and data organization.

Skills and Attributes
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy when coding transactions and performing reconciliations.
  • Ability to manage multiple client deadlines and prioritize tasks in a fast‑paced environment.
  • Comfortable working with checklists, documented procedures, and standardized workflows.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Collaborative mindset and openness to feedback, coaching, and learning new systems.
  • High level of integrity and respect for client confidentiality.

Work Environment and Growth
  • Collaborative, tech‑forward firm focused on Client Accounting Services and fractional finance support.
  • Training and mentorship from Staff Accountants and CAS leadership, with opportunities to grow into a Staff Accountant role over time.
  • Exposure to multiple industries and clients, with increasing responsibility as skills and judgment develop.
  • Remote role - candidates must be based in Mexico.
  • Compensation dependent on experience ($1500 - $2500/month)

Proof is the world's first identity-assured transaction management platform and we are on a mission to digitize trust for all of life’s most critical transactions. Developed by the same market leaders and experts who brought notarization online with Notarize℠, Proof offers trust in a digital world by verifying identities and securing transactions to protect businesses and their customers. Proof operates identity infrastructure for high-consequence transactions. Built on a WebTrust-audited certificate authority and PKI-anchored verifiable credentials, Proof helps more than 8,000 businesses, from financial institutions and mortgage lenders to insurers and wealth managers, verify who is on the other side of a transaction. Having created the online notarization category, we're now extending into portable digital identity with our Verifiable Digital Credential (VDC) for banks, and into authorization for AI agents.

As Director of Product Marketing, you'll turn that technical foundation into positioning that a bank's Chief Risk Officer, head of digital, and compliance team all understand and act on. Day to day, you'll work across Product, Sales, and Marketing to shape messaging, lead launches, equip Sales to win, and make sure the market sees Proof as the trusted identity layer. You'll also lead and develop the product marketing function, starting with the Partner & Customer Marketing Manager.

  • Launches and go-to-market: Run the launch process for new products and major features, from tiering and readiness through announcement, enablement, an post-launch measurement. Shape use-case plays such as account opening, high-value money movement, title and closing, and agent-initiated transactions with Revenue Marketing and Sales.
  • Sales enablement: Build and maintain the core sales toolkit, including pitch decks, solution briefs, discovery guides, business-case and ROI tools, objection handling, and demo narratives. Run ongoing enablement for Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and partners.
  • Market and competitive insight: Lead win/loss analysis, customer interviews, persona and buying-committee research, and competitive intelligence across identity verification, digital credentials, eSignature, and fraud prevention vendors, including maintained battlecards.

jobs.title: Manager of Business Analytics - Non-Prime Installment Loan
jobs.excerpt: At Koalafi, we believe in a world where no one has to put an important purchase on hold.
jobs.description:
At Koalafi, we believe in a world where no one has to put an important purchase on hold. That’s why we’re making it easier for more people to pay for big purchases over time.

Retailers across the country rely on us to offer flexible lease-to-own financing to their non-prime consumers, while increasing sales and strengthening customer loyalty. Their 2M+ customers love us because we provide a flexible way for them to make payments and give them an opportunity to improve their credit. Our 200+ Koalafi teammates enjoy inspiring and challenging work that accelerates their careers.

Interested in learning more about how we’re transforming the financing experience and joining our team?

What You’ll Do

Koalafi is expanding beyond lease-to-own by launching a non-prime installment loan product that will diversify our portfolio and accelerate growth in select states and verticals. The Manager of Business Analysis will report directly to the Chief Risk Officer and play a central role in designing and operationalizing the company’s risk management framework for this new product. The role will lead development of core risk policies (credit, fraud, KYC/AML, collections, etc.), build a robust monitoring and reporting suite, and execute ad hoc analyses that support product development, pilot rollout, and scaling. This person will be a key cross-functional partner to Product, Engineering, Compliance/Legal, Operations, and Finance.

Risk Policy Development & Governance

  • Lead drafting and iteration of risk management policies and standards supporting the non-prime installment product, including:
    • Credit policy (eligibility, underwriting strategy, line assignment, and pricing inputs)
    • Fraud policy (identity theft, synthetic fraud, first-party fraud, and merchant abuse)
    • KYC / identity verification standards (CIP/KYC requirements, documentary verification requirements, third-party data use, and step-up verification)
    • Servicing and collections risk policy (hardship, restructures, settlements, and outbound communications)
  • Translate policy intent into operational procedures and control requirements
  • Establish a lightweight governance cadence for policy review/changes and maintain a living policy repository with change logs

Monitoring Suite & Risk Reporting

  • Design and implement a monitoring framework for the new product that includes:
    • Risk appetite metrics and early-warning indicators (origination mix, approval rates, early DQ, roll rates, fraud rate, payment failure rates, complaint rate, etc.)
    • Cohort/vintage tracking and performance segmentation (state, vertical, channel, merchant, score band, income/DTI bands, etc.)
    • Operational controls monitoring (KYC pass rates, step-up rates, manual review queues, etc.)
  • Build a recurring executive reporting pack for the leadership team and create self-serve dashboards for day-to-day decision making.
  • Partner with Analytics and Data Engineering to ensure data definitions are consistent, auditable, and scalable (metric dictionary, QA checks, reconciliation vs. source systems).

Product Launch Support & Ad Hoc Analysis

  • Support product design decisions by quantifying trade-offs among risk, approval rate, unit economics, and customer experience (e.g., pricing sensitivity, repayment term structures, down payment requirements, etc.).
  • Conduct targeted analyses to inform rollout strategy by state and vertical, including regulatory-driven constraints and operational readiness.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering on test design and evaluation (A/B tests, pilots, phased rollouts), including measurement plans and success criteria.

Cross-Functional Influence & Execution

  • Serve as a primary risk analytics partner to Product/Engineering during build, ensuring risk requirements are embedded in workflows (application, underwriting, funding, servicing, and collections).
  • Collaborate closely with Compliance/Legal to translate regulatory requirements into operational policy and monitoring.
  • Coordinate with Operations to ensure procedures, training, and escalation pathways align with policy intent.
  • Drive clarity in decision-making: define owners, timelines, and expected deliverables; keep stakeholders aligned through launch milestones.

What Success Looks Like (First 6–12 Months)

  • Core risk policies for the installment product are drafted, approved, and operationalized with clear change-control and exception processes.
  • A “first-class” monitoring suite is live with daily/weekly dashboards and a monthly executive risk review cadence.
  • Leadership has clear visibility into product performance by state/vertical, with early-warning signals and action plans.
  • Policy and monitoring enable a controlled rollout that meets regulatory needs while achieving target approval and loss-rate ranges.

About You (Qualifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree required, in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Business, or Engineering preferred
  • 5+ years of experience in an analyst, data science, or consulting role
  • 3+ years of experience in credit risk analytics
  • Experience in consumer financing industry, such as credit cards, personal loans, auto loans, BNPL, or similar field
  • Proficiency in Excel, SQL, and Python for data analysis
  • Exceptional attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Ability to create a strategic agenda and execute against it
  • Desire to work in a fast-paced, dynamic entrepreneurial environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

Location: Richmond, VA; Arlington, VA; or Remote (U.S.). Associates near one of our office locations may work in-office, hybrid, or remotely. Remote opportunities are available to candidates throughout the United States.

Salary Range: $131,000-$165,000 per year (depending on experience and location)
Additional Compensation: This position is eligible to participate in company bonus plan.

The final salary offer will depend on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and geographic location. The actual annualized salary amount offered to any candidate at the time of hire will be reflected solely in the candidate’s offer letter.

Applications will be accepted until position is filled.

Why choose Koalafi: A career at Koalafi means opportunities to tackle exciting challenges every single day. We take pride in a culture of innovation, trust, and ownership. You'll get outside your comfort zone, build meaningful relationships, and most of all, take charge of projects that ultimately help people get the things they need most.

Benefits:

At Koalafi, you will have a direct impact on our products and help shape the company’s success. We offer competitive compensation & benefits packages to keep you at your best:

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 20 PTO days + 11 paid holidays
  • 401(k) retirement with company matching
  • Student Loan & Tuition Reimbursement
  • Commuter assistance
  • Parental leave (maternal + paternal)
  • Inclusion and Associate Engagement Programs

Who we are & what we value:

  • We focus on what’s most important
  • We set clear expectations and deliver
  • We embrace challenges to reach our full potential
  • We ask, “How can this be better?”
  • We move fast together

jobs.excerpt: Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage.
jobs.description:
Cresta unlocks the true potential of the customer experience, turning every conversation into a competitive advantage. Cresta’s unified AI platform combines conversational AI agents, real-time human agent augmentation, and comprehensive conversation intelligence to drive revenue and efficiency gains across every channel. The world’s leading companies, including United Airlines, Cox Communications, and Marriott, use Cresta to power world-class customer experiences every day.

Born from the Stanford AI Lab, Cresta has raised more than $270 million from the world’s leading investors, including a16z, Greylock, and Sequoia. Cresta’s leadership includes some of the leading minds in AI today. Our CEO, Ping Wu, founded and led Google's Contact Center AI and Vertex AI platforms before joining Cresta to build the future of AI-driven customer experiences.

Over the next few years, AI is going to redefine how people all over the world interact with businesses every day. Come build that future at Cresta.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Event & Field Marketing Manager – East / Central to join Cresta’s Revenue Marketing team. This role owns strategy, execution, and performance across a high-volume portfolio of field marketing programs — from industry events and executive dinners to regional programs, roadshows, customer experiences, and partner activations.

This isn’t an events-for-events-sake role. Field Marketing is a meaningful pipeline channel at Cresta, and you’ll partner closely with Sales to determine where we invest, which accounts and audiences we target, and how programs contribute to pipeline creation and acceleration.

You’ll typically own 8–10+ programs per quarter and be responsible for taking them from initial strategy through execution, Sales follow-up, measurement, and optimization.

Location: This is a remote role supporting our East region. We strongly prefer candidates currently based on the U.S. East Coast, but are open to candidates in the Central U.S. who can easily support Eastern time zones and regional travel. This role requires approximately 20–30% travel, with heavier travel during peak event seasons.

Responsibilities

  • Own Field Strategy + Execution: Build and execute field marketing programs aligned to regional Sales priorities, target accounts, and pipeline goals.
  • Drive Pipeline + ROI: Set program KPIs, track sourced and influenced pipeline, measure conversion and ROI, and translate results into clear recommendations.
  • Partner Closely with Sales: Work with Sales before, during, and after programs on account targeting, attendance, meetings, follow-up, and opportunity acceleration.
  • Manage a High-Volume Portfolio: Own 8–10+ programs per quarter across tradeshows, executive dinners, roadshows, customer programs, regional activations, and partner events.
  • Own Programs End-to-End: Manage strategy, budgets, vendors, contracts, promotion, attendee experience, onsite execution, and post-event reporting.
  • Make Smart Investment Decisions: Evaluate program performance, forecast spend, identify trade-offs, and shift investment toward the programs driving the strongest business impact.
  • Build Integrated Campaigns: Partner with Demand Gen, Digital, Product Marketing, Partnerships, and Sales to drive attendance and engagement across target accounts.
  • Create Standout Experiences: Bring new ideas and formats to the table that differentiate Cresta and create meaningful experiences for customers and prospects.
  • Build Repeatable Playbooks: Develop processes and workflows that allow the field marketing motion to scale as Cresta grows.
  • Support Executive Programs: Partner with Cresta executives and Sales leaders on messaging, speaker preparation, executive experiences, and customer engagement.

Qualifications

  • 3–5+ years of B2B field marketing, regional marketing, event marketing, or integrated campaign experience
  • Experience owning field programs end-to-end, from strategy through execution and measurement
  • Comfortable managing 8–10+ concurrent programs per quarter in a fast-moving environment
  • Strong understanding of pipeline, revenue attribution, conversion, and event ROI
  • Proven experience partnering directly with Sales on account targeting, program strategy, and follow-up
  • Experience managing program budgets, vendors, contracts, and competing priorities
  • Strong communicator who can work effectively across Sales, Marketing, executives, agencies, and external partners
  • Currently based in the Eastern or Central U.S., with a strong preference for East Coast
  • Willing and able to travel approximately 20–30%

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a high-growth B2B SaaS or startup environment
  • Experience with AI, Contact Center, Customer Experience, or adjacent enterprise technology
  • Experience supporting enterprise or strategic Sales teams
  • Experience with ABM/account-based field marketing programs
  • Previous Sales/SDR experience or strong understanding of enterprise Sales processes
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, and field marketing/event tools such as Mobly

Perks & Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision plans designed to fit you and your family’s needs
  • Flexible vacation time to support a healthy work-life blend
  • Paid parental leave
  • Monthly gym and phone allowance
  • Work-from-home office stipend
  • Lunches and dinners for in-office employees via Grubhub

Compensation at Cresta

Cresta’s approach to compensation is simple: recognize impact, reward excellence, and invest in our people. We offer competitive, location-based pay that reflects the market and what each individual brings to the table.

The posted base salary range represents what we expect to pay for this role in a given location. Final offers are shaped by factors including experience, skills, education, and geography. In addition to base salary, total compensation includes equity and a comprehensive benefits package.

Salary Range: $110,000–$150,000 base + equity

Our use of AI in recruiting: We may use AI tools in our recruiting process, which require human review and oversight. If you have questions about our use of AI or wish to opt out, please contact (if you are opting out, please use the subject ‘Opt-Out’ in your email).
Recording & AI transcription: We do not authorize candidates to record or use AI transcription of any interview by phone, notetaker app, AI glasses, or other device. Candidates may request an exception or accommodation for review during the interview process as needed.
Recruiting impersonation scams: We have noticed a rise in recruiting impersonations across the industry, where scammers attempt to access candidates' personal and financial information through fake interviews and offers. All Cresta recruiting email communications will always come from the @cresta.ai domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Cresta via other sources should be ignored.

Expected Travel: Up to 10%

Ingenyx proudly launched as a new, independent company following its divestiture from Teleflex on August 3, 2026.

Ingenyx is a leading global provider of product development and production services for medical device manufacturers. We set ourselves apart with deep expertise, decades of experience, a dedication to design for manufacturability, and extensive, in-house capabilities, which include engineering, regulatory services, material selection and formulation, prototyping, manufacturing, assembly and packaging. We deliver industry-changing innovations and next-generation solutions for extrusions; diagnostic and interventional catheters; balloons and balloon catheters; sheath/dilator sets; specialty sutures, braids and fibers; and bioabsorbable sutures, yarns and resins. Join a dynamic, growing team that offers healthcare providers an array of medical technology solutions that make a difference in patients’ lives.

For more information, please visit

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Post-Market Surveillance, Vigilance & Complaints Lead to manage global post-market activities for medical devices for which the company is a Legal Manufacturer.
This role is responsible for complaint handling, vigilance and adverse event reporting, post-market surveillance, signal detection and trending, and Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSURs). The Lead will serve as the primary subject matter expert for post-market regulatory requirements and partner closely with Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Risk Management, Engineering, Operations, and external clinical experts.
This senior individual contributor/functional leadership role requires strong technical expertise, regulatory judgment, and the ability to lead cross-functional activities across a global organization.

Principal Responsibilities

  • Lead complaint handling process for Legal Manufacturer products, ensuring complaints are appropriately documented, investigated, assessed, and closed.
    • Oversee complaint investigations carried out by manufacturing sites, suppliers, contract manufacturers, and technical experts while maintaining Legal Manufacturer accountability.
    • Lead global vigilance and reportability assessments and ensure adverse event reports are submitted within applicable timelines.
    • Lead the global Post-Market Surveillance program, including PMS Plans/Reports, complaint trending, signal detection, and evaluation of emerging safety or performance issues.
    • Own the PSUR process from planning and compilation through cross-functional review and timely completion.
    • Ensure post-market information is appropriately incorporated into product risk management, CAPA, Management Review, and other Quality System processes.
    • Provide complaint, vigilance, and PMS data for CER, PMCF, SSCP, PSUR, and other clinical evidence activities.
    • Partner with Regulatory Affairs, which retains ownership of clinical evidence strategy, CER/CEP governance, PMCF strategy, SSCP governance, clinical vendor management, and final manufacturer approval.
    • Support evaluation and execution of field actions, recalls, corrections/removals, FSCAs, and other product safety actions, as applicable.
    • Serve as the primary complaint/PMS/vigilance subject matter expert during regulatory inspections, Notified Body audits, and MDSAP audits.
    • Monitor evolving global post-market and vigilance requirements and support implementation of applicable regulatory changes.

Education / Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, or a related technical or scientific discipline.
    • 8+ years of medical device industry experience in complaint handling, PMS, vigilance, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, or related post-market functions, including 5+ years of direct post-market experience.
    • Demonstrated experience with medical device complaint investigations and regulatory reportability assessments.
    • Strong knowledge of EU MDR PMS and vigilance requirements, including PSURs, PMS Reports, trend reporting, and vigilance.
    • Working knowledge of FDA Medical Device Reporting requirements and global post-market regulations.
    • Experience with complaint trending, signal detection, and integration of post-market data into ISO 14971 risk management.
    • Experience supporting regulatory inspections, Notified Body audits, and/or MDSAP audits.
    • Strong analytical, technical writing, communication, and cross-functional leadership skills.

Specialized Skills / Other Requirements

  • 10+ years of medical device industry experience.
    • Experience leading global complaint handling, PMS, or vigilance programs for a Legal Manufacturer.
    • Experience with post-market requirements in the U.S., EU, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan, Brazil, and Switzerland.
    • Experience preparing and leading PSURs; experience supporting CER, PMCF, and SSCP activities.
    • Experience working with external Medical Directors, clinical consultants, biostatisticians, or other specialized clinical resources.
    • RAC, ASQ, or equivalent professional certification.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means development of a sustainable, inspection-ready post-market program with timely complaint handling and reporting, effective signal detection, high-quality PMS/PSUR deliverables, and strong integration with risk management and clinical evidence.

jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

Role Type: Full-time
Location: Remote (U.S.)
Reports To: Head of People
Comp: $110,000 - $150,000

About Claude Corps

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career talent in nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions those organizations can continue using after the fellowship ends. It is a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance. Fellows are full-time employees for a one-year term.

Cohorts now run in the hundreds, and new fellows onboard while earlier cohorts are still placed. We need an HR partner who can support fellows and their managers year-round and run onboarding at that scale.

About the role

You are the HR partner to Claude Corps program leaders and the AI Practice Leads who manage fellows day to day. You will own onboarding quality and deadlines for each cohort while Sr People Operations Coordinator, reporting to you, runs the day-to-day execution.

Your focus shifts throughout the year. As a cohort prepares to start, you spend more time running onboarding and completing the work alongside the Sr. People Operations Coordinator. Once fellows are placed, you spend more time advising managers, addressing employee concerns, and supporting performance. New cohorts will onboard while earlier cohorts are still working, so you will need to balance both responsibilities.

This is a senior, hands-on role. You bring sound judgment to employee situations, help managers address issues early, and build clear processes as the program grows. You work closely with the Head of People, the recruiting team, program leaders, Finance, and our HR service providers.

As onboarding volume grows, you identify when additional support is needed, define that work, and train and oversee the people helping deliver it. You remain accountable for onboarding quality and deadlines.

What you’ll do

Partner with program leaders and managers

  • Advise program leaders and AI Practice Leads on performance, employee concerns, role expectations, and team needs, and help managers set clear expectations and address problems early
  • Clarify who owns what between fellow managers, host organizations, and the program team when employee questions arise
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend changes to manager guidance, policies, or how the program operates

Manage employee relations and performance issues

  • Handle employee concerns with care and consistency: gather the facts, document clearly, and bring significant issues and recommended actions to the Head of People
  • Guide managers through performance conversations, improvement plans, and conduct issues
  • Manage leave and accommodation requests with the appropriate providers and advisors

Own fellow onboarding

  • Run onboarding for each cohort, from signed offer through the employment steps needed to start: background checks, I-9 and work authorization, employee records, payroll setup, and benefits enrollment
  • Confirm work locations and coordinate state notices and employment documents
  • Send clear instructions, track each fellow’s progress, and work with recruiting and program teams to resolve missing information, changes, and delays
  • Complete onboarding tasks directly, check that records and setup are accurate, and keep employment onboarding aligned with orientation and cohort start dates

Plan and oversee onboarding support

  • Manage the Senior People Operations Coordinator: set priorities by cohort, review their work, and keep sensitive questions and decisions with the right HR owner
  • Plan onboarding workload against cohort size, deadlines, and support needed for current fellows, and flag when volume requires surge help
  • Build checklists and repeatable processes so larger cohorts onboard with less manual work

Support fellows throughout the year

  • Be an HR contact for questions about benefits, leave, workplace concerns, and employment policies
  • Help managers and fellows resolve timekeeping issues and coordinate payroll corrections with Finance and our providers
  • Maintain accurate employee records as work locations or employment details change
  • Coordinate fellowship completion, early departures, and offboarding
  • Track recurring questions and improve guidance so fellows and managers know what to do

Maintain policies and employment practices

  • Keep the Fellow Handbook, manager guidance, and state supplements current with the Head of People and appropriate advisors
  • Coordinate multistate employment requirements and help managers understand the rules for hourly, nonexempt employees
  • Apply policies consistently and seek legal or specialized advice when a situation calls for it

Improve HR processes and reporting

  • Track onboarding readiness, open tasks, and employee issues, and give the Head of People clear updates on risks, workload, and recommended actions
  • Use approved AI tools and automation to cut repetitive work in communications, tracking, and reporting, while checking accuracy and protecting employee information

Requirements

  • At least seven years of progressive HR experience, including time as an HR business partner advising managers on performance, conduct, and sensitive employee situations
  • You have personally run onboarding at volume and can move between advising leaders and doing the operational work
  • You have supported employees across multiple states, including hourly, nonexempt employees
  • You understand how HR records, payroll, benefits, leave, and onboarding connect. PEO experience is a strong plus
  • You have managed or trained staff doing HR or onboarding work
  • You can build structure in a growing program while handling overlapping deadlines and day-to-day employee needs
  • You communicate clearly, document well, and know when to involve the Head of People or a specialist
  • You have improved HR processes using technology, AI, or automation

Key success metrics

  • Onboarding readiness: Fellows complete required employment steps on time, with accurate records and payroll and benefits setup
  • Manager support: Managers receive practical guidance and address performance and employee concerns promptly
  • Employee relations: Issues are handled consistently, documented clearly, and escalated at the right time
  • Balanced delivery: New cohorts onboard on schedule while current fellows and managers continue receiving timely HR support
  • Onboarding capacity: Support needs are identified early, assignments are clear, and work is checked for quality
  • Employment practices: Policies, records, and state requirements stay current, with gaps addressed promptly
  • Process improvement: Manual work and recurring errors decrease as cohort size grows

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position’s level, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re hiring for a Senior level position at an annual salary of $110,000 to $150,000. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

  • Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection
  • Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)
  • Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support
  • ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt
  • Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

jobs.description:
Position: Vollzeit (40h)

Ort: Remote (Deutschland) oder Berlin

Start Datum: Ab sofort oder nach Absprache

Sprachen: Deutsch & Englisch

Du willst Verantwortung für den CRM-Umsatz übernehmen und mit deinem Team dafür sorgen, dass unsere Kundinnen immer wieder zu Maniko zurückkommen?

Wenn du Lust hast, aus Erstkäuferinnen loyale Stammkundinnen zu machen, unsere Retention Engine mit Automatisierung, Segmentierung und Personalisierung auf das nächste Level zu bringen und dabei ein Team zu führen, dann ist diese Rolle perfekt für dich. Als Teamlead CRM & Retention (all genders) verantwortest du CRM und Retention bei Maniko, von der Strategie bis zur Umsetzung in Klaviyo.

Das sind wir!

Maniko ist ein innovatives, schnell wachsendes Unternehmen in der Nagelkosmetik-Branche, das hochwertige Produkte für anspruchsvolle Kundinnen europaweit anbietet. Wir sind bekannt für unsere selbstklebende UV Gel Nail Strips-Technologie, die professionelle Ergebnisse bequem von zu Hause aus ermöglicht, und haben mit unseren Soft Gel Press-On Nails eine zweite starke Produktlinie im Markt.

Unsere Produkte stehen national bei dm, dm Österreich, Rossmann und budni im Regal, und wir verkaufen direkt über unseren Online-Shop in Deutschland, Frankreich und Italien. Aus dem einst kleinen Startup ist ein Unternehmen geworden, das mit den großen Beauty-Marken konkurriert. Groß genug, dass deine Flows und Kampagnen jeden Tag eine große Community erreichen, und flexibel genug, dass du unsere Retention Engine selbst baust, statt sie nur zu verwalten.

Unser Geheimnis? Ein leidenschaftliches Team, das sich nicht mit dem Status quo zufrieden gibt und ständig danach strebt, besser zu werden. Wir glauben an Werte, die wirklich gelebt werden, keine leeren Phrasen. Bei uns heißt es:

  • Facts over Ego: Daten und Ergebnisse stehen über allem. Bei uns zählt das Beste für das Team und das Unternehmen, nicht das persönliche Ego.

  • Challenge accepted: Wir sehen in jeder Herausforderung eine Chance, an der wir wachsen können.

  • Power to the people: Vertrauen und Verantwortung gehen bei uns Hand in Hand. Dein Impact zählt!

  • Who if not you?: Wenn nicht du die Ärmel hochkrempelst und Dinge anpackst, wer dann?

Requirements

Deine Rolle bei uns:

Du führst unser CRM-Team mit drei direkten Reports und verantwortest neben E-Mail auch unser Loyalty-Programm und das Community-Management unserer Facebook-Community. Deine CRM- und Lifecycle-Strategie entwickelst du gemeinsam mit unserem Head of Growth weiter, und mit unserem Senior Performance Marketing Manager sorgst du dafür, dass Paid und CRM ineinandergreifen. Deine Rolle ist strategisch und klar operativ zugleich. Du trägst die Verantwortung für den CRM-Umsatz, und dein Erfolg ist messbar: an Wiederkaufrate, Umsatz pro Empfänger und CLV.

Deine Aufgaben sind:

  • Du entwickelst unsere CRM- und Lifecycle-Strategie weiter, planst die CRM-Roadmap und setzt sie um, vom Erstkauf bis zur loyalen Kundin.

  • Du verantwortest den CRM-Umsatz und steuerst nach klaren Zielen wie Wiederkaufrate, Umsatz pro Empfänger, Kohortenentwicklung bzw. CLV und Abmelderate.

  • Du konzipierst, baust und optimierst automatisierte Flows in Klaviyo, von Welcome und Post-Purchase über Replenishment und Cross-/Upselling bis Win-back.

  • Du entwickelst eine granulare Segmentierung nach Lifecycle-Stufe, Kaufverhalten und Produktaffinität, etwa zwischen UV Gel Nail Strips und Soft Gel Press-On Nails, und personalisierst Inhalte und Angebote entlang der gesamten Customer Journey.

  • Du planst Newsletter und Kampagnen und setzt sie hands-on in Klaviyo um, in enger Abstimmung mit Brand & Content. KI-Tools wie Claude nutzt du für Copy, Briefings und Kampagnenproduktion.

  • Du fährst strukturierte A/B-Tests mit klaren Hypothesen, entscheidest nach Umsatz pro Empfänger und analysierst Kohorten.

  • Du automatisierst Reportings und wiederkehrende CRM-Prozesse und stellst eine saubere, DSGVO-konforme Datenbasis sicher.

  • Du entwickelst unser Loyalty-Programm und unsere Facebook-Community als Hebel für Wiederkauf weiter und spielst Insights an Brand, Product und Growth zurück.

  • Du führst unser CRM-Team direkt und entwickelst es fachlich und disziplinarisch weiter.

Was du mitbringst:

  • Klaviyo-Expertise: Du hast mehrjährige Hands-on-Erfahrung in CRM, Lifecycle oder Retention Marketing im D2C-E-Commerce und kennst Klaviyo in der Tiefe: komplexe Flows, Segmentierung, Templates und Testing. Deine Flows kannst du im Detail erklären, weil du sie selbst gebaut hast.

  • Track Record: Du hast Wiederkaufrate, CLV und CRM-Umsatzanteil nachweislich gesteigert und kannst das mit Zahlen belegen.

  • Führung: Du hast Erfahrung darin, ein CRM-Team zu führen, und setzt dabei weiterhin selbst um.

  • Branchenerfahrung: Du kommst aus dem D2C-E-Commerce, idealerweise aus einer Beauty-Marke, alternativ aus vergleichbaren Kategorien wie Supplements oder Health.

  • Commercial Drive: Du denkst in Umsatz pro Empfänger, CLV und Deckungsbeitrag, baust aus unterschiedlichen Segmentierungslogiken eine Retention Engine und verstehst, wie CRM, Brand und Performance zusammenspielen.

  • Tools & KI: Du arbeitest sicher mit Shopify-Integrationen, hast ein fundiertes Verständnis von DSGVO und Datenschutz und setzt KI-Tools wie Claude souverän im CRM-Workflow ein.

  • Arbeitsweise: Du führst mit klarer Richtung und packst selbst mit an. Du kommunizierst offen und klar, im Team wie gegenüber dem Management, auch wenn etwas nicht funktioniert. Du fühlst dich in einer schnellen Taktung mit iterativen Entscheidungen wohl, triffst eigenständig Entscheidungen und übernimmst Verantwortung dafür.

  • Sprachen: Du sprichst sehr gutes Deutsch und Englisch.

Idealerweise bringst du außerdem mit:

  • Erfahrung mit Loyalty-Programmen und Community-Management.

  • Starke Copywriting-Skills, idealerweise aus einer früheren Rolle.

Was wir dir bieten:

  • 🇪🇺 100 % Remote in Deutschland: Remote-first mit optionalem Büro in Berlin.

  • ⏱️ Flexible Arbeitszeiten: Somit kannst du privates und berufliches flexibel und entspannt vereinbaren.

  • 🚉 Deutschlandticket: Für mehr Flexibilität und Mobilität.

  • 🏃‍♀️ Urban Sports Club Membership: Weil wir wissen, wie wichtig physische Gesundheit und Ausgleich ist.

  • 🤝 Ownership: Durch viel Vertrauen & Gestaltungsspielraum hast du direkten Einfluss auf den Erfolg unseres Unternehmens und gestaltest maßgeblich unser Wachstum mit.

  • 🌴 Workation: Deine Möglichkeit Urlaub und Arbeit zu verbinden.

  • 📈Wachstumschancen: Sowohl persönlich als auch beruflich. Bei uns kannst du dich weiterentwickeln und neue Wege gehen, unterstützt durch ein jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget.

  • 🎉 Team-Events: Wir laden alle Mitarbeiter:innen regelmäßig nach Berlin ein, um eine gute Zeit zusammen zu haben und noch besser connecten zu können.

  • 🖥️ Home-Office Ausstattung: Wir übernehmen deine komplette Ausstattung, damit du auch zu Hause direkt durchstarten kannst.

  • 👥 Team: Ein schnelles, hochmotiviertes Team mit Office im Herzen von Berlin (Hackescher Markt).

  • ✨Eine Kultur, die inspiriert: Bei uns zählt jeder Einzelne. Flache Hierarchien, schnelle Entscheidungen und echte Teamarbeit stehen im Mittelpunkt.

Challenge accepted? Dann bewirb dich jetzt und werde Teil eines Teams, das große Ziele verfolgt und dabei nie den Spaß verliert.

Wir freuen uns auf dich!

jobs.excerpt: Director of Research OperationsClinical Research | Multi-Site Research NetworkPosition SummaryWe are seeking an experienced Director of Research Operations to lead the day-to-day operational execution of a growing, multi-site clinical trials portfolio.
jobs.description:
Director of Research Operations

Clinical Research | Multi-Site Research Network

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Director of Research Operations to lead the day-to-day operational execution of a growing, multi-site clinical trials portfolio.

Reporting to the Vice President of Research, the Director will translate the organization’s research strategy and growth objectives into consistent, measurable operational execution across the clinical trials enterprise.

This role is responsible for the operational foundation of clinical trial delivery: ensuring studies move efficiently from award through startup, activation, recruitment, enrollment, conduct, and closeout; sites have the resources and support required to perform; operational teams work cohesively across functional areas; and leadership has clear visibility into performance, risks, and resource needs.

The Director will lead and coordinate the functional areas supporting clinical trial execution, including site operations, study startup and activation, regulatory operations, recruitment and enrollment, trial delivery and project management, research systems and training, and operational data and performance management.

This is an execution-focused leadership role. Enterprise research strategy, organizational growth strategy, executive and sponsor relationships, research portfolio development, financial and business oversight, quality governance, and expansion of new research service lines remain under executive research leadership. The Director of Research Operations will be responsible for ensuring that those strategic priorities are translated into effective day-to-day clinical trial operations.

The successful candidate will be a highly experienced clinical research operations leader who knows how to build structure, establish accountability, develop teams, solve operational problems, and create scalable processes without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Clinical Trial Operations

  • Own the operational execution of the clinical trials portfolio from study award through closeout.

  • Translate organizational priorities into clear operational plans, responsibilities, timelines, and performance expectations.

  • Create consistent operating practices across centralized research functions and participating research sites.

  • Maintain visibility into the health of the clinical trial portfolio, including startup progress, enrollment performance, operational milestones, staffing and workload, and significant risks or barriers.

  • Ensure issues are identified early, assigned to the appropriate owner, escalated when necessary, and followed through to resolution.

Drive Site Performance & Operational Excellence

  • Ensure research sites have the infrastructure, processes, staffing support, training, and centralized resources necessary to execute clinical trials successfully.

  • Establish clear expectations for site performance and routinely evaluate operational readiness, workload, enrollment performance, study execution, and barriers to success.

  • Partner with site and practice leadership to address operational challenges while maintaining appropriate accountability for performance.

  • Balance network-wide standardization with the practical needs of individual practices, investigators, and studies.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce duplication, and improve the experience of conducting research within participating practices.

Oversee Study Startup & Activation

  • Drive efficient movement of studies from award through site activation.

  • Ensure coordination of regulatory activities, site readiness, systems setup, training, investigator preparation, operational planning, and other startup requirements.

  • Establish measurable startup expectations and monitor studies against those expectations.

  • Identify recurring causes of activation delays and implement process improvements to address them.

Strengthen Recruitment, Screening & Enrollment

  • Ensure effective operational processes for identifying, screening, and enrolling appropriate research participants.

  • Coordinate centralized recruitment resources with site-based recruitment and clinical-practice workflows.

  • Strengthen integration of clinical research into routine patient care so that investigators and clinical teams can effectively identify potential participants.

  • Establish visibility into recruitment funnels and enrollment performance and ensure underperforming studies have actionable recruitment plans.

  • Drive follow-through and accountability for enrollment initiatives.

Establish Strong Trial Delivery & Project Management

  • Create consistent project-management standards across active studies.

  • Ensure studies have appropriate operational plans, timelines, meeting structures, deliverables, action-item tracking, escalation pathways, and communication processes.

  • Establish clear ownership of study activities and ensure commitments to sponsors, investigators, sites, and internal stakeholders are tracked through completion.

  • Develop processes that allow leadership to identify studies requiring intervention before significant milestones are missed.

Integrate Regulatory Operations into Trial Delivery

  • Ensure regulatory activities are effectively integrated into startup and ongoing study operations.

  • Maintain efficient processes for submissions, essential-document management, investigator documentation, amendments, continuing reviews, and closeout activities.

  • Ensure regulatory workload and timelines are visible within overall study planning.

  • Partner with quality and compliance leadership to address operational findings and ensure corrective actions are translated into sustainable operational practices.

Optimize Research Systems, Technology & Training

  • Ensure research technology supports efficient trial execution across the network.

  • Drive effective adoption and utilization of clinical trial management, electronic source, electronic regulatory, recruitment, and other research platforms.

  • Identify workflow or technology barriers that create unnecessary administrative burden and lead efforts to improve them.

  • Ensure research staff receive appropriate onboarding, systems training, role-based training, and ongoing operational education.

  • Identify opportunities to appropriately use technology, automation, data, and artificial intelligence to improve research operations.

Build Operational Visibility & Accountability

  • Develop and maintain meaningful operational metrics related to study startup, enrollment, trial performance, site performance, staffing, workload, and delivery.

  • Use data to identify trends, anticipate operational needs, and guide resource allocation.

  • Establish regular operating reviews that move beyond reporting information to identifying decisions, owners, actions, and deadlines.

  • Provide executive research leadership with concise, reliable visibility into operational performance, significant risks, resource requirements, and issues requiring executive intervention.

Lead & Develop the Research Operations Team

  • Build a high-performing, collaborative research operations organization with clear responsibilities and accountability.

  • Ensure functional teams operate as an integrated clinical trials organization rather than as independent operational silos.

  • Develop leaders and team members who can independently solve problems, make appropriate decisions, and take ownership of outcomes.

  • Evaluate workload and staffing requirements as the portfolio grows and recommend resource changes based on operational demand.

  • Create a culture characterized by ownership, responsiveness, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

Decision-Making & Leadership Scope

The Director of Research Operations will have significant authority over the day-to-day execution of clinical trial operations and will be expected to independently make operational decisions within established organizational strategy, policies, budgets, and quality standards.

The Director will determine how operational resources are deployed, how workflows are structured, how operational issues are resolved, and when performance concerns require intervention or escalation.

The role will partner closely with executive research leadership on matters involving significant financial commitments, organizational strategy, sponsor or executive relationships, major staffing investments, research portfolio decisions, quality or compliance risk, and expansion into new research capabilities or service lines.

The expectation is not simply to identify operational problems for executive leadership to solve. The Director should arrive with an assessment, a recommended solution, and a plan for execution, escalating primarily when a decision requires executive authority or has broader organizational implications.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means the clinical research organization operates effectively and predictably as the research network grows.

Studies move from award to activation efficiently. Sites know what is expected of them and have access to the support they need. Recruitment opportunities are identified and acted upon. Enrollment performance is actively managed. Operational risks are identified early. Teams understand who owns what. Commitments are followed through to completion. Leadership can quickly understand the health of the portfolio.

Most importantly, day-to-day clinical trial operations do not require continuous executive intervention to move forward.

The Director creates the structure, leadership, operating discipline, and accountability that allow executive research leadership to remain focused on strategy, growth, partnerships, financial performance, organizational development, and the future direction of the research enterprise.

Qualifications

Required

  • Extensive clinical research experience with progressive responsibility in research operations and leadership.

  • Demonstrated experience overseeing clinical trial execution across multiple studies, sites, or research programs.

  • Strong operational knowledge of study startup, regulatory processes, recruitment and enrollment, trial conduct, and study closeout.

  • Experience leading teams and coordinating work across multiple functional areas.

  • Demonstrated ability to build operational processes and establish accountability in a growing or changing organization.

  • Strong understanding of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and sponsor-supported clinical trial operations.

  • Demonstrated ability to identify complex operational problems, develop practical solutions, and drive implementation through completion.

  • Strong project-management, organizational, and prioritization skills.

  • Ability to interpret operational data and use it to drive decisions and performance improvement.

  • Strong leadership and communication skills with the ability to work effectively with investigators, research staff, clinical practices, sponsors, CROs, and executive leadership.

Preferred

  • Experience within a multi-site clinical research organization, healthcare network, site network, or similarly distributed research environment.

  • Experience building or scaling clinical research operations.

  • Experience supporting cardiovascular or other complex therapeutic-area clinical trials.

  • Experience implementing or optimizing centralized research services.

  • Experience with clinical trial management systems, electronic source, electronic regulatory systems, recruitment technologies, and other research platforms.

  • Experience developing operational dashboards, KPIs, and performance-management processes.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to take operational leadership of a growing clinical trials organization at an important stage in its development.

We have built the foundation. The next challenge is creating the operational structure and discipline that allow the organization to scale.

We are looking for a leader who can see both the individual trial and the operating system behind it — someone who can move comfortably between people, processes, sites, systems, and data; recognize where execution is breaking down; and then take ownership of fixing it.

The right person will not simply manage clinical research operations. He/she will build an organization that consistently delivers successful clinical trials.

jobs.excerpt: Crystalia Glass LLC is a U. S. -based manufacturer and provider of premium glass solutions, specializing in custom glass partitions for residential, commercial, and institutional projects.
jobs.description:
Crystalia Glass LLC is a U.S.-based manufacturer and provider of premium glass solutions, specializing in custom glass partitions for residential, commercial, and institutional projects. We operate a full-cycle model — from design and manufacturing to sales, delivery, and installation — with production facilities in the United States and Europe.

The U.S. market is our core focus. Crystalia Glass is a stable, scaling business, serving B2C, B2B, and B2G clients across multiple states. We combine strong product quality, competitive pricing, high service standards, and operational efficiency to set a benchmark within our industry.

We are strengthening our commercial function and are looking for a Sales Enablement Manager to own the quality of sales execution across the full funnel, from first contact and needs discovery to closing and order handover.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. Sales Enablement Manager will diagnose why deals are lost, coach sales teams, build and adapt sales standards and CRM stage logic, and embed AI into everyday sales work. Success depends on driving adoption across sales teams and measuring real change in sales representatives’ behavior and conversion.

Employment Type:

- Full-time 8.30 am - 5 pm, NY (EST zone).

- Remote work.

- B2B contract (sole proprietorship status or corporate entity).


Key responsibilities:

Analyze performance

  • Review won, lost and stalled deals across funnel stages, matching calls and messages against CRM history and using AI to flag missed questions, weak arguments, unhandled objections and missing next steps.
  • Assess each sales stage (discovery, qualification, value presentation, objection handling, negotiation, closing and follow-up), including how scripts are adapted to the client and whether call goals are achieved.
  • Identify root causes of performance gaps (skills, knowledge, process or tools) and recommend targeted fixes.

Develop the team

  • Run one-to-one and team call and deal reviews, role-plays (including AI-simulated buyers and objections), live call observation and product knowledge checks.
  • Build individual development plans and coach sales representatives on specific sales behaviors.
  • Coach team leads to apply shared quality criteria in daily work with their teams.

Track results

  • Track whether new behaviors and AI workflows are applied in real deals and how they affect conversion, deal outcomes and time spent.

Standards and CRM

  • Audit existing sales standards for gaps, contradictions and requirements that don’t help the sale.
  • Write and update sales standards: scripts, objection guides, follow-up rules, contact quality criteria and product instructions, as well as CRM stage rules — the goal, entry and exit criteria, required data, sales representative actions and next steps for each stage, ownership at handover, and SLAs agreed with the process owner (response time, working hours, exceptions and escalation).
  • Pilot and roll out new standards: incorporate feedback from sales representatives and team leads, agree commercial rules with sales leadership, write requirements for CRM fields, prompts, notifications, reports and automation, take part in acceptance testing, and train sales representatives after changes.
  • Monitor adherence to standards in the CRM: overdue tasks, missing next steps, unconfirmed stage moves, missing loss reasons and handover quality.

AI in sales work

  • Build reusable AI workflows for sales representatives and team leads (call and meeting preparation, meeting summaries, follow-up messages, discovery question planning and checking proposals against client and product data), train sales teams to use them, observe real usage and fix errors.
  • Work with AI agents and bots; maintain instructions, templates and knowledge-base materials.
  • Use AI to help sales representatives plan next steps in the CRM, making sure they review every AI-drafted message or data update before it goes to a client or changes key deal information.

Build enablement assets

  • Build and maintain the team skills map, call and deal scorecard, prioritized list of loss reasons and a library of examples and exercises.

Requirements
